pl-l4d36c1-d1e115.summary: Turns to whether condition can divide marriage.

pl-l4d36c1-d1e118.summary: Answers that a free woman may marry a slave, but if his servile condition was unknown, she may freely dismiss him when it is discovered; according to the rule: if a free man takes another's slave as wife thinking her free, and she is later found to be a slave, he should redeem her if he can; if not, he may take another; if he knew and approved, he must keep her as lawful.

pl-l4d36c1-d1e127.summary: Adds: if a free woman knowingly married a slave, she must keep him, since we all have one Father in heaven and there is one law for man and woman. 'Knowingly' implies that if she did not know, she is not bound to remain; if deceived about condition she need not cling to the deceiver; but if either knew the other's condition, there is no dismissal.
claims: Knowing marriage to a slave binds.
Fraud about condition frees the deceived.

pl-l4d36c1-d1e137.summary: Cites Pope Zachary: a free man who married a slave with mutual consent may not dismiss her except for fornication; this concerns those whose conditions were known at marriage.
claims: Knowingly contracted marriage with a slave is indissoluble.

pl-l4d36c1.summary: Asks whether condition can divide marriage. A free woman may marry a slave, but if unaware of his servile condition she may dismiss him when it is discovered; a free man who married a slave thinking her free may redeem her or take another, but if he knew, he must keep her. Pope Zachary forbids a free man to dismiss a slave wife he married knowingly with mutual consent, except for fornication.
claims: Free persons may validly marry slaves.
Error about servile condition allows separation.
Knowing marriage to a slave is indissoluble.
